children: JGBs rise in price terms in early Tokyo session amid artificial-intelligence-related credit concerns. "[We are] watching whether [these concerns] could serve as a catalyst for investors to move away from the excessive avoidance of duration risk, having favored credit and spread risk over duration risk," two members of J.P. Morgan's Japan Markets Research say in a research report. "Assuming the recent credit concerns do not develop into a major risk-off episode, we maintain our view that excessive rate hike pricing will first be unwound at the front end, followed by a decline in longer-term yields, they add. Ten-year JGB yield is down 2.5 bps at 2.905%. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
